title: Geometric morphisms of topoi and their 2-morphisms
statement: Let $\mathcal E,\mathcal F$ be categories. A geometric-morphism datum $f:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$ consists of functors $f^{-1}:\mathcal F\to\mathcal E$ and $f_*:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, an adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$, and preservation of finite limits by $f^{-1}$. When $\mathcal E,\mathcal F$ are Grothendieck topoi [def-weil-pbc-topos] in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention], this is a geometric morphism of topoi. For geometric morphisms $a:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$ and $b:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$, their composite has inverse image $a^{-1}b^{-1}$ and direct image $b_*a_*$, with the composite adjunction. A $2$-morphism $f\Rightarrow g$ is a natural transformation $f_*\to g_*$. Its inverse-image mate is the corresponding transformation $g^{-1}\to f^{-1}$ under adjunction; a direct-image natural isomorphism gives its corresponding inverse-image natural isomorphism.
